Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Solutions Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Morrison, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Janet Morrison, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to StellarTech Solutions’ Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Ramsey, CEO; David Chen, CFO; Sarah Jenkins, COO; and Mark Olsen, CTO.
Earlier today, we issued our earnings press release and presentation, which are available on our Investor Relations website. Please note this call may include forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to Alex Ramsey.

Alex Ramsey, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet. Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining us.

This quarter, we saw meaningful progress across several fronts.

To start, Samsung Electronics delivered a strong Q3 2024 performance, showcasing resilience and strategic execution across its diverse business portfolio. Company-wide revenue reached KRW 79.1 trillion, representing a 7% sequential increase compared to Q2 2024 and a 12% year-over-year (YoY) improvement. This performance exceeded our guidance from last quarter, which projected revenue in the range of KRW 76-78 trillion. This outperformance can be attributed to a confluence of factors, including stronger-than-anticipated smartphone demand, a rebound in high-end memory product sales, and robust display panel orders related to key customer product launches.
This reflects, most notably, the Mobile eXperience (MX) business which emerged as the primary growth driver in Q3, recording an impressive 13% sequential revenue increase. This translates to approximately KRW 32.8 trillion in revenue compared to KRW 29 trillion in Q2. The catalyst for this growth was undoubtedly the successful launch of the latest flagship smartphone models, the Galaxy S24 series and the foldable Z Fold 6 and Z Flip 6. Specifically, pre-order numbers for the Z Fold 6 and Z Flip 6 exceeded internal projections by 25%, indicating strong consumer appetite for innovative foldable technology. We estimate that the foldable category contributed approximately KRW 8.5 trillion to MX revenue in Q3, demonstrating its increasing significance. Furthermore, the mid-range A series continued to perform well in emerging markets like India and Southeast Asia, contributing a significant volume of sales and offsetting some of the softness observed in developed markets. From a regional perspective, North America and Europe showed moderate growth, driven by carrier promotions and bundled deals centered around the new flagship devices. However, the Asia-Pacific region (excluding China) witnessed the most substantial growth, driven by pent-up demand after a relatively sluggish H1. The launch of exclusive color variants and targeted marketing campaigns in these regions further fueled sales. Strategically, Samsung’s continued focus on AI integration within its mobile devices is proving to be a key differentiator. The Galaxy AI suite, featuring real-time translation, enhanced photography capabilities, and intelligent battery management, has resonated well with consumers and is contributing to higher average selling prices (ASPs). We believe that Samsung's investment in on-device AI processing and cloud-based AI services will be crucial for sustaining its competitive edge in the long term. The Device Solutions (DS) business, encompassing memory, system LSI, and foundry, recorded a 3% sequential revenue increase, reaching approximately KRW 25.8 trillion. While this growth is less pronounced than the MX business, it represents a significant improvement compared to the previous two quarters, signaling a gradual recovery in the memory market. The primary driver of this growth was increased sales of high-end memory products, particularly DDR5 DRAM and high-bandwidth memory (HBM), driven by the demand for AI servers and data centers. We estimate that HBM sales more than doubled compared to Q2, contributing approximately KRW 4.5 trillion to the DS revenue. This reflects Samsung's success in securing key partnerships with leading AI accelerator manufacturers, including NVIDIA and AMD. While the overall memory market is still facing challenges related to oversupply and price pressure, Samsung’s strategic focus on high-value, cutting-edge memory solutions is enabling it to outperform its competitors. Furthermore, the System LSI division saw increased demand for its 5G modem and image sensor solutions, particularly for automotive and industrial applications. The foundry business, while still facing headwinds, benefited from increased capacity utilization and the ramp-up of new process technologies. Samsung's continued investment in advanced process nodes, including 3nm and 2nm GAA (Gate-All-Around) technology, is crucial for attracting new customers and securing long-term growth in the foundry market. We anticipate a more pronounced recovery in the foundry business in 2025 as the industry navigates the current semiconductor cycle. Finally, the display business booked a 5% sequential revenue increase, reaching approximately KRW 8.5 trillion. This growth was primarily driven by increased orders from major customers, particularly Apple and Samsung's own MX division, for OLED panels used in new smartphone and tablet models. The launch of the iPhone 16 series, featuring Samsung-supplied OLED panels, contributed significantly to the display business's revenue in Q3. Furthermore, Samsung's continued leadership in foldable display technology resulted in increased demand for its flexible OLED panels used in the Galaxy Z Fold 6 and Z Flip 6. While the LCD market remains competitive, Samsung's strategic shift towards high-value OLED panels is proving to be a successful strategy. The company's investment in QD-OLED technology is also yielding positive results, with increased adoption in premium TV models. As mentioned, our initial guidance for Q3 revenue was in the KRW 76-78 trillion range. The actual revenue of KRW 79.1 trillion exceeded this projection due to the following reasons: Stronger-than-anticipated smartphone demand, as the initial forecast was based on more conservative projections for the adoption of the Z Fold 6 and Z Flip 6, and the overwhelmingly positive consumer response led to significantly higher sales than anticipated. There was also a faster recovery in high-end memory, as the demand for HBM and DDR5 memory products for AI applications accelerated faster than initially predicted. This was partially driven by unexpected announcements from leading AI companies expanding their data center infrastructure investments. Lastly, favorable currency exchange rates, while not a primary driver, the weakening of the Korean Won against the US Dollar and other major currencies provided a slight tailwind to reported revenue.

We also continued to drive improvements through our CapEx guidance. As previously indicated, we are revising our full-year 2024 CapEx guidance upwards. We now anticipate total capital expenditures of KRW 56.7 trillion, an increase of approximately KRW 3.6 trillion from our prior guidance of KRW 53.1 trillion issued at the end of Q1. This adjustment reflects evolving market dynamics and strategic imperatives across our businesses, particularly in the display sector. Within the Device Solutions (DS) segment, Memory CapEx is expected to be largely in line with the previous year's spend of KRW 38.5 trillion. While the overall figure remains consistent, the allocation within Memory is shifting. We are strategically re-prioritizing investments towards advanced DRAM technologies, specifically focusing on HBM3e and DDR5. This includes securing critical EUV lithography equipment and expanding cleanroom capacity in our Pyeongtaek Line 3 and Xi'an Line 2 facilities. We anticipate a 12% increase in CapEx dedicated to HBM3e production compared to our initial plans, driven by surging demand from AI accelerator manufacturers. This shift comes partially at the expense of investments in older DRAM nodes, where we are optimizing existing capacity rather than pursuing aggressive expansion. We saw a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion from HBM sales alone, confirming our strategic direction. We are also piloting a new advanced packaging technology, "HyperCube," which will require an incremental investment of approximately KRW 500 billion over the next two years, starting with initial deployments in Q4 of this year. While not directly reflected in this year's CapEx, it represents a significant long-term investment commitment. Our Foundry division is projecting a decrease in annual CapEx compared to last year's record high. We now forecast Foundry CapEx at KRW 9.4 trillion, down from KRW 11.2 trillion in 2023. This reduction does *not* signal a lack of commitment to the Foundry business. Instead, it reflects a more judicious allocation of resources following a period of aggressive expansion and technology node development. We've completed the initial build-out of our Taylor, Texas facility, and are now focusing on ramping up production and optimizing yields. The current guidance reflects a slowdown in spending on additional equipment for the Taylor fab, and instead, an increase in investment into advanced packaging technologies to better fulfill customer demand for chiplets and heterogeneous integration. We are seeing strong interest in our 4nm and 3nm process technologies, especially from North American customers in the HPC and automotive sectors. We are delaying the full deployment of the 2nm node until the second half of 2025 to ensure adequate process maturity. This strategic pause allows us to refine our manufacturing processes and address early customer feedback. While memory and foundry have some changes, the overall CapEx for DS is slightly down to KRW 47.9 trillion. This decrease reflects a strategic shift towards greater efficiency and targeted investments in key growth areas. The most significant driver of the increased CapEx guidance is our Display division. We now expect Display CapEx to reach KRW 5.6 trillion, significantly higher than last year's total of KRW 3.8 trillion. This increase is primarily driven by two factors: (1) a substantial investment in QD-OLED panel technology for next-generation TVs and monitors, and (2) expansion of flexible OLED production capacity to meet growing demand from the mobile and automotive sectors. Specifically, we are investing KRW 2.5 trillion in upgrading our Gen 8.5 QD-OLED manufacturing line, which is expected to begin mass production in Q3 2025. This upgrade will improve panel efficiency, color gamut, and overall image quality. Furthermore, we are allocating KRW 1.8 trillion to expand flexible OLED production capacity at our A3 and A4 lines, specifically targeting the foldable smartphone market and automotive display applications. We project a 30% increase in flexible OLED shipments in 2025, driven by new product launches from key customers. We are also exploring microLED technology, but large-scale CapEx investments in this area are not anticipated until 2026 or beyond. In Q2, memory investments were focused on securing long-lead-time equipment for HBM3e and DDR5 production. We saw a slight increase in CapEx related to EUV lithography tools, reflecting the growing complexity of advanced DRAM manufacturing. Q2 Foundry CapEx was primarily directed towards the Taylor, Texas fab, with significant spending on infrastructure and initial equipment installations. We are on track to begin initial production at the Taylor facility in the first half of 2025. Display CapEx in Q2 centered on the procurement of equipment for the Gen 8.5 QD-OLED upgrade. We also made progress on expanding flexible OLED production capacity. Our long-term CapEx strategy is predicated on several key assumptions: Continued growth in AI and HPC, so we expect strong demand for high-performance memory and advanced packaging solutions to continue, driven by the growth of AI and HPC applications. We also anticipate continued growth in the flexible OLED market, particularly in the mobile and automotive sectors. We remain committed to maintaining technology leadership in our core businesses, which requires ongoing investments in R&D and advanced manufacturing capabilities. Lastly, we are closely monitoring geopolitical developments and adjusting our CapEx plans accordingly. We are diversifying our manufacturing footprint and strengthening our supply chain to mitigate potential risks. Our CapEx investments are strategically allocated across our global manufacturing footprint. We are expanding capacity in South Korea, China, and the United States to meet growing demand and diversify our geographic exposure. We are also exploring potential investments in Southeast Asia, particularly in Vietnam and Malaysia.

Lastly, I want to briefly highlight the sales by segment. Q3 FY24 performance demonstrates solid growth and profitability, driven by a strategic focus on flagship products within the MX division and sustained demand in the Larger Display business. While macroeconomic headwinds persist, targeted product positioning and efficient supply chain management have allowed us to exceed internal projections. We shipped 58 million smartphones in Q3, representing a 12% increase compared to Q3 FY23 (51.8 million units). This growth was primarily fueled by robust demand for our flagship "Galaxy Zenith" series and mid-range "Galaxy Horizon" lineup, specifically, the Galaxy Zenith accounted for 22 million units shipped, while the Galaxy Horizon contributed 28 million units. The remaining 8 million units comprised of older models and entry-level devices. Tablet shipments reached 7 million units, a 5% decrease year-over-year (7.4 million units in Q3 FY23). This slight decline reflects the ongoing industry-wide softening in tablet demand, partially offset by successful promotions targeting the back-to-school season. Our smartphone ASP stood at $295, a 10% increase compared to $268 in Q3 FY23. This significant improvement is attributed to a higher proportion of flagship sales and successful pricing strategies implemented across the Zenith and Horizon lines. The Zenith's ASP hovered around $550, while the Horizon maintained an ASP of $280. Older models averaged around $150. The MX division recorded Q3 revenue of $18.6 billion, a 15% increase year-over-year. Smartphone sales contributed approximately $17.1 billion, while tablet sales accounted for $1.5 billion. The MX division achieved a gross margin of 32.5% in Q3, up from 29.8% in Q3 FY23. This improvement is primarily driven by the increased smartphone ASP and efficient cost management within our manufacturing facilities. We achieved an operating margin close to 10%, specifically 9.8%, exceeding our internal target of 9%. This reflects the higher gross margin and effective control of operating expenses. We are seeing improvements with our shift away from low-margin products. North America, Europe, and parts of Asia have shown the most positive trends, reflecting the strongest demand for flagship models. Emerging markets continue to be important for volume, but generally contribute to lower margins. Also, sales volume of TVs increased by 8% compared to Q2 FY24, driven by robust demand for our premium QLED and OLED models. Monitor sales volume increased by 5% sequentially, fueled by stable demand from both consumer and commercial segments. The gaming monitor sub-segment continued to show strong growth. The Larger Display business recorded Q3 revenue of $6.2 billion, a 3% increase compared to Q2 FY24. The TV segment contributed approximately $4.1 billion, while the monitor segment accounted for $2.1 billion. The Larger Display business achieved a gross margin of 26% in Q3, slightly down from 26.5% in Q2 FY24. This marginal decrease reflects increased competition in the TV market and higher input costs. Operating margin remained relatively stable at 6.5%. We are continuing to focus on cost optimization and premium product positioning to maintain profitability in this segment.

Now I’ll hand it over to David Chen to discuss the financials in greater detail.

David Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Alex, and good day, everyone.

From a financial perspective, we’re pleased with the breadth and durability of our results.

First, our reported gross margin for Q3 2024 landed at 37.9%. While this remains a healthy margin overall, it represents a decline of 200 basis points (2 percentage points) sequentially, compared to the 39.9% reported in Q2 2024. Year-over-year (YoY), we see a more modest decrease of 0.8 percentage points from Q3 2023's 38.7%. This performance also falls short of our guidance of 38.5% provided during the Q2 2024 earnings call.
Inventory valuation reversals and aging inventory depletion has contributed meaningfully to this. In Q2 2024, we benefited from a substantial reversal of previous inventory write-downs, contributing approximately 1.5 percentage points to the gross margin. These reversals were primarily related to raw material cost decreases across our Asian manufacturing facilities, specifically impacting our Component X and Polymer Y product lines. However, in Q3 2024, these reversals were significantly lower, contributing only 0.3 percentage points. This shift alone accounts for a 1.2 percentage point drag on the QoQ gross margin. The primary reason for this decline in reversals is that raw material costs have stabilized, removing the opportunity for the same write-down reversals we saw in Q2. We anticipate this trend to continue into Q4 2024, suggesting that inventory valuation reversals are unlikely to be a significant tailwind in the near term. As part of our ongoing efforts to optimize working capital and reduce inventory obsolescence, we proactively implemented a strategy to deplete aging inventories, particularly within our North American distribution network. This involved targeted promotional campaigns and strategic price reductions on older product lines. While this initiative successfully reduced our overall inventory holding costs and improved cash flow, it negatively impacted our gross margin. We estimate the impact of this aging inventory depletion to be approximately 0.8 percentage points. A specific example is our Legacy Model 7000 product line in the US market, which experienced a 20% price reduction to accelerate sales and clear existing stock. While this boosted unit sales by 35% for that product line, the lower margin per unit contributed to the overall QoQ decline. While the QoQ performance was negatively affected, the YoY decline of only 0.8 percentage points indicates underlying operational improvements that partially offset the challenges. We attribute this to continued investments in automation and process optimization at our European production facilities led to a 3% reduction in manufacturing costs per unit. This was particularly noticeable in our Premium Series Z product line. We are rolling out similar initiatives across our other facilities and expect further efficiency gains in the coming quarters. This accounted for approximately 0.5 percentage points of gross margin improvement YoY. Strategic partnerships with key suppliers and improved demand forecasting allowed us to negotiate better pricing on certain raw materials, specifically for our Advanced Material Compound (AMC). This initiative shaved off roughly 2% of our direct material costs compared to the same period last year. This contributed around 0.3 percentage points to the gross margin YoY. The launch of our new Innovative Edge series of products, with enhanced features and a premium price point, has gained strong traction in the market, particularly in the Asia-Pacific region. The Innovative Edge series carries a gross margin profile 5 percentage points higher than our average. The increased sales mix of these products contributed approximately 0.4 percentage points to the gross margin YoY. However, these positive factors were offset by increased freight costs, as global freight rates, particularly ocean freight, have increased significantly due to geopolitical instability and port congestion. This added approximately 0.5 percentage points to our cost of goods sold (COGS) compared to last year. There were also unfavorable currency movements, specifically the strengthening of the US dollar against the Euro and Japanese Yen, negatively impacted our international sales and sourcing costs. This had a marginal impact of approximately 0.5 percentage points on our gross margin. As mentioned earlier, our Q3 2024 gross margin of 37.9% fell short of our initial guidance of 38.5%. The 60-basis point difference primarily stems from an underestimation of the impact of aging inventory depletion. During our Q2 earnings call, we projected a more gradual depletion of aging inventories, anticipating a lesser impact on gross margin. However, due to increased competitive pressures and the need to accelerate inventory turnover, we implemented more aggressive promotional strategies, resulting in lower average selling prices. We had projected the impact of aging inventory depletion to be approximately 0.3 percentage points; however, the actual impact was 0.8 percentage points, adding 0.5 percentage points to the miss. Additionally, we experienced higher-than-anticipated freight costs associated with expediting shipments to meet increased demand in key markets, especially North America. This added an additional 0.1 percentage point impact to the miss, for a total of 0.6 percentage points.

Second, we saw negative contribution from our operating margin results. For Q3 2024, our operating margin landed at 11.6%, a decrease of 2.5 percentage points compared to the 14.1% achieved in Q2 2024.
Increased raw material costs, ramp-up costs for the "Project Phoenix" automation initiative and increased sales & marketing spend, which all contributed to the quarter-over-quarter decrease. We experienced a surge in the cost of key raw materials, specifically polymer resins used in our industrial coatings division. The global polymer resin index climbed by approximately 8% during Q3, primarily due to supply chain disruptions stemming from geopolitical instability in the Middle East. This directly impacted our COGS, contributing an estimated 1.2 percentage point reduction in our operating margin. We mitigated some of this impact through strategic hedging, which prevented a potentially larger drop of closer to 1.8 percentage points. As previously communicated, we are heavily investing in automation across our manufacturing facilities under the "Project Phoenix" initiative. Q3 saw the peak of implementation in two of our largest North American plants. While these automation efforts are expected to yield significant cost savings in the long run (estimated at $35 million annually starting in 2025), the short-term impact includes increased depreciation expenses, training costs, and initial operational inefficiencies as systems are brought online. This contributed approximately 0.8 percentage points to the operating margin decline. In Q3, we strategically increased our sales and marketing expenditure by 12% compared to Q2, representing a $15 million increase. This investment was primarily focused on launching our new line of eco-friendly consumer paints in the European market. Although early indicators are promising, with initial sales exceeding projections by 7%, the increased marketing spend negatively impacted the Q3 operating margin by approximately 0.5 percentage points. We anticipate these investments will pay off in subsequent quarters as the product gains traction. Despite the QoQ decline, our operating margin improved by 0.8 percentage points compared to the 10.8% reported in Q3 2023. This positive YoY trend is primarily attributable to the volume growth in key segments. We witnessed a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion. This growth was fueled by strong performance in our automotive coatings division, which benefited from the resurgence in global automotive production. Additionally, our infrastructure coatings segment experienced a 12% YoY revenue increase, driven by government infrastructure spending in North America and Europe. The price increases implemented in late 2023 across select product lines have begun to positively impact our margins. While these price increases faced initial resistance from some customers, the overall impact has been positive, contributing approximately 1.5 percentage points to the YoY operating margin improvement. Over the past year, we've focused on optimizing our distribution network by consolidating regional warehouses and implementing improved logistics management systems. These initiatives have resulted in a reduction in distribution costs, contributing roughly 0.3 percentage points to the YoY margin improvement. These gains were partially offset by the raw material cost increases described earlier, as well as increased employee compensation, reflecting a tight labor market. In our Q2 2024 earnings call, we provided operating margin guidance of 13.5% to 14.5% for Q3 2024. The actual result of 11.6% falls short of this guidance. The reasons for this miss are multifaceted: While we anticipated some inflationary pressure on raw materials, the severity of the increase, particularly in polymer resins, exceeded our initial projections. Our initial models projected a 3% increase in the global polymer resin index, but the actual increase was closer to 8%. This variance alone accounts for approximately 0.8 percentage points of the guidance miss. We initially projected a more rapid ramp-up of the "Project Phoenix" automation initiative, with some initial cost savings anticipated to materialize in Q3. However, unforeseen technical challenges and integration complexities delayed the realization of these benefits. This resulted in higher-than-expected implementation costs and a slower-than-anticipated reduction in labor costs. Unfavorable currency exchange rate fluctuations, particularly the strengthening of the US dollar against the Euro, negatively impacted our reported operating margin. While our hedging strategies mitigated some of this impact, the magnitude of the currency movements was greater than anticipated, contributing approximately 0.2 percentage points to the guidance miss.

And although still early, sales guidance is showing some positive trends. We anticipate a generally positive trajectory heading into Q4 2024 and a more robust outlook for FY2025. While certain segments face headwinds, the overall market demand is expected to trend positively, particularly driven by AI and data-related infrastructure investments. We project a 7% sequential increase in revenue for the semiconductor business compared to Q3 2024, reaching approximately $18.5 billion. This improvement is primarily driven by the DS (Device Solutions) division, offsetting anticipated softness in mobile and PC segments. AI and the explosive growth of data are expected to fuel strong demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and enterprise-grade SSDs. We anticipate a 15% increase in HBM sales, contributing approximately $3.8 billion to the overall DS revenue. This is partially offset by continued softness in the consumer memory market. We expect a 5% decrease in mobile DRAM sales due to inventory corrections and pricing pressures. We are strategically focusing on Gen6 HBM3e technology, which is expected to ramp up production in Q4, securing key design wins with leading AI accelerator manufacturers like NVIDIA and AMD. We are also seeing increased adoption of our DDR5 memory in data center environments, contributing to a 12% increase in server DRAM sales. Our Foundry business is a critical focus, with a commitment to increase order volume by enhancing the competitiveness of our advanced technologies. In Q4, we are targeting a 3% increase in Foundry revenue, reaching approximately $5.2 billion. This growth is predicated on securing new design wins for our 4nm and 5nm processes in applications like automotive SoCs and high-performance computing. We are actively investing in EUV lithography to improve yields and reduce costs in our advanced nodes. We are also seeing increasing interest in our GAA (Gate-All-Around) technology, with initial pilot production slated for late Q4 and commercial availability planned for early 2025. We believe GAA will be a significant differentiator in the long term, particularly in the power-sensitive mobile and HPC markets. Competitively, TSMC remains a significant competitor, but we are actively working to close the gap through technology innovation and strategic partnerships. We anticipate a double-digit growth for the semiconductor business in FY2025, with revenue exceeding $80 billion. This will be driven by broad-based strength across the market, especially high-end memory and Foundry services. Display is expected to perform strongly, with a projected 12% increase in revenue compared to Q3 2024, reaching approximately $9.2 billion. This growth is driven by robust demand for our OLED panels in flagship smartphone models from major customers like Apple and Samsung. We anticipate a significant uptick in sales of flexible OLED panels for foldable devices, contributing approximately $1.8 billion. We are also seeing healthy growth in the IT and automotive display sectors. Demand for high-resolution displays in gaming monitors and premium laptops is expected to increase by 8% in Q4. Our automotive display sales are projected to grow by 15%, driven by the increasing adoption of OLED technology in electric vehicles and advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS). We are actively working on developing transparent OLED displays for automotive applications, which we believe will be a key differentiator in the future. We expect continued growth in the Display segment in FY2025, with a focus on expanding our presence in the automotive and IT markets. We are forecasting a 7% revenue growth overall for FY2025. We anticipate a slight decline in DX (Device eXperience) sales compared to Q3 2024, approximately 2%, reaching $45.8 billion. This is primarily due to seasonality and a slight slowdown in consumer electronics demand following the holiday season. We are taking actions to mitigate this decline, including promotional campaigns and new product launches. Within the DX division, we are seeing continued strong demand for our premium smartphones, particularly the Galaxy S and Fold series. However, the overall smartphone market is becoming increasingly competitive, with intense price pressure from Chinese manufacturers. We are focused on differentiating our products through innovative features, such as enhanced AI capabilities and improved camera technology. We are also investing in the development of new form factors, such as rollable displays, to maintain our competitive edge. We expect the DX division to return to growth in FY2025, driven by the launch of new flagship products and the expansion of our ecosystem of connected devices. We are forecasting a 3% revenue growth for FY2025. We anticipate strong growth in North America, driven by demand for AI infrastructure and premium consumer electronics. We expect moderate growth in Europe, with a focus on automotive and industrial applications. China remains a challenging market, with intense competition and regulatory uncertainties. We are focused on maintaining our market share by offering differentiated products and services. We see significant growth potential in emerging markets, particularly in Southeast Asia and India. We are investing in expanding our sales and distribution network in these regions.

With that, I’ll turn it to Sarah Jenkins for a deeper look at operational performance.

We’re also seeing early traction in our wafer sales. As previously reported, our foundry's overall earnings for Q3 2024 declined by 8% compared to Q2 2024, landing at $1.93 billion. While we saw a healthy 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, the bottom line was significantly impacted by a one-off cost of approximately $180 million. This includes a $110 million charge related to a special employee incentive program implemented to retain key talent in the face of increased competition, and a $70 million inventory provision for engineering run wafers. This provision primarily stems from obsolescence and lower yields observed in our advanced 3nm and 5nm process node development. We shipped a total of 850,000 300mm equivalent wafers this quarter, a slight decrease of 2% compared to the 867,000 wafers shipped in Q2 2024. This slight dip is directly attributable to the engineering run wafer provisions, as some of these wafers were deemed unsaleable and written down. Shipments of mature nodes (90nm and above) remained relatively stable, accounting for approximately 35% of total wafer shipments. We saw continued strong demand from the automotive and industrial sectors for these nodes. Specifically, 180nm technology used in power management ICs experienced a 5% increase in shipment volume due to robust demand in Electric Vehicles (EVs). aspect_summary.Revenue results, QoQ changes, YoY change: Company-wide revenue reached KRW 79.1 trillion, a 7% sequential increase compared to Q2 2024 and a 12% YoY improvement. This exceeded the previous guidance of KRW 76-78 trillion due to stronger smartphone demand, a rebound in high-end memory sales, and robust display panel orders.
aspect_summary.CapEx guidance for the full year or long: Full-year 2024 CapEx guidance is revised upwards to KRW 56.7 trillion, an increase of KRW 3.6 trillion from the previous guidance. Memory CapEx is expected to be in line with the previous year, but allocation shifts towards advanced DRAM technologies like HBM3e and DDR5. Foundry CapEx is projected to decrease, reflecting a more judicious allocation of resources. Display CapEx is significantly higher due to investments in QD-OLED and flexible OLED production. Long-term CapEx strategy is predicated on continued growth in AI/HPC and the flexible OLED market.
aspect_summary.sales by segment or platforms, their res: The Mobile eXperience (MX) business recorded a 13% sequential revenue increase, driven by the launch of new flagship smartphones. The Device Solutions (DS) business saw a 3% sequential revenue increase, driven by high-end memory products. The display business booked a 5% sequential revenue increase, driven by OLED panel orders. MX division achieved a gross margin of 32.5% and an operating margin of 9.8%. The Larger Display business achieved a gross margin of 26% and an operating margin of 6.5%.
aspect_summary.Gross margin results, QoQ changes, YoY c: The reported gross margin for Q3 2024 was 37.9%, a decline of 200 basis points sequentially and 0.8 percentage points YoY. This fell short of the guidance of 38.5%. The QoQ decline was due to lower inventory valuation reversals and aging inventory depletion. The YoY decline was partially offset by investments in automation, strategic partnerships, and the launch of new products.
aspect_summary.Operating margin results, QoQ changes, Y: The operating margin for Q3 2024 was 11.6%, a decrease of 2.5 percentage points QoQ but an increase of 0.8 percentage points YoY. It fell short of the guidance of 13.5% to 14.5%. The QoQ decrease was due to increased raw material costs, ramp-up costs for automation, and increased sales and marketing spend. The YoY improvement was primarily attributable to volume growth and price increases.
aspect_summary.sales guidance, forecast, or trend by se: A generally positive trajectory is anticipated for Q4 2024 and FY2025. A 7% sequential revenue increase is projected for the semiconductor business. Display is expected to perform strongly, with a projected 12% increase in revenue compared to Q3 2024. A slight decline in DX sales is anticipated compared to Q3 2024. A 7% revenue growth overall is forecasted for FY2025.
